item.title: Pantethine Shows Potential as Supplement for Psoriasis Treatment
item.description: Scientists from China have discovered that pantethine, a vitamin B5 derivative commonly available as a nutritional supplement, may help combat psoriasis by calming overactive immune cells. The research, published in the Journal of Experimental Medicine, reveals an unexpected connection between cholesterol metabolism and autoimmune inflammation. In mouse models, pantethine prevented psoriasis development, while a small human trial involving 24 patients showed improved symptoms when combined with standard topical treatments. The study found that dendritic cells in psoriasis patients exhibited unusually high levels of Vanin enzymes, which convert pantethine into vitamin B5. When Vanin activity was reduced, dendritic cells became less active, reducing their ability to stimulate T cells and trigger inflammation. item.title: Ancient Marine Ecosystem Reveals New Model of Evolutionary Transition Without Mass Extinction
item.description: A groundbreaking fossil discovery in Colombia's Paja Formation is reshaping scientific understanding of evolutionary transitions. Researchers from McGill University and the Centro de Investigaciones Paleontológicas (CIP) have identified an exceptionally diverse marine ecosystem from the Early Cretaceous period that coexisted with declining Jurassic lineages and emerging Cretaceous groups. This previously unrecognized pattern, termed a 'Biotic Inflection,' challenges the long-held belief that major evolutionary changes require mass extinction events. The Paja Biota, as researchers call this community, includes giant marine reptiles like long-necked plesiosaurs, marine crocodile relatives, turtles, sharks, and crustaceans, forming one of the most ecologically complex marine communities ever documented. item.title: Traditional Serbian custom of placing stones in home corners for winter protection observed on Mitrovdan
item.description: The article discusses a traditional Serbian custom observed in the Šumadija region during Mitrovdan, a holiday dedicated to Saint Dimitrius. According to the article, families in Šumadija place small stones, known as 'belutak' or 'oblutak,' in every corner of their homes on Mitrovdan. This practice, rooted in folk belief, was intended to protect homes from mice during winter. The article explains that Mitrovdan marks the transition from warm to cold weather, signaling the start of winter preparations. Before Mitrovdan, farmers were expected to complete outdoor work, move livestock indoors, and prepare homes and storage areas for the colder months. The custom of placing stones in corners was based on the belief that these stones would create an invisible barrier in areas where mice typically hide and travel, thus safeguarding food supplies. Peak travel dates, which include most of November, all of December, the first half of January, and 11 days in February, now carry higher fees of $55/$70 for the first bag. The second checked bag fee has also increased to $70/$75 for off-peak travel and $75/$85 for peak dates. Under the new structure, checking one bag both ways on a round-trip peak-day itinerary could cost up to $140 without prepayment. Free checked bag allowances still apply for premium fares, Mosaic-level TrueBlue loyalty program members, and JetBlue credit card holders. The film follows Petey, a man who formed a deep bond with an alien named Allen during his childhood, only to lose him suddenly. Decades later, Petey remains fixated on recapturing that magical connection, mirroring Pearson's own experience after his older brother Liam died of cancer at age 26. Pearson has not previously spoken publicly about his brother's death, but the film has become a way for him to process his grief. 'He was the best thing ever to me,' Pearson says of his brother, emphasizing how the loss shaped his attachment to childhood pop culture. item.title: How Optimizing Nginx and Cloudflare Configuration Reduced Cloud Run Data Transfer Costs by 96%
item.description: The author of a personal blog hosted on Google Cloud Run discovered significant cost savings by reviewing and optimizing their nginx and Cloudflare configurations. Previously, their monthly Google Cloud bill had exceeded ¥1,000 for about a year, but after implementing two key changes, it dropped to ¥72 in October. The primary issue was that nginx gzip compression was disabled, causing Cloud Run to send uncompressed data to Cloudflare, which was then billed as data transfer. By enabling gzip compression, the size of the index.xml feed (which accounted for over 90% of data transfer) was reduced from 5.4 MB to 1.27 MB. Additionally, the author configured Cloudflare to cache HTML content and the index.xml feed, which reduced the number of requests to Cloud Run. Before the changes, Cloud Run data transfer costs were ¥556 in September, but after optimization, they dropped to ¥24 in October, representing a 96% reduction. item.description: Macquarie Island, located approximately 1,000 kilometers from the nearest landmass, is a unique geological site that allows visitors to walk directly on the Earth's mantle. This remote island, situated between Tasmania and Antarctica, is the only place on the planet where the mantle is exposed at the surface. The island's geological significance stems from its position on a 1,600-kilometer-long underwater fault line between the Australian and Pacific tectonic plates. Unlike most locations where mantle material is only accessible through volcanic activity or deep drilling, Macquarie Island provides direct access to the mantle due to its unique tectonic setting. The island has a rich history of human interaction, including early European exploration in the early 19th century, a period of intense hunting of seals and penguins for their oil, and later becoming a scientific research site. item.title: Surgical Resection Preferred Over SABR for Early-Stage NSCLC in Medically Suitable Patients, Study Finds
item.description: A large population-based study published in the Journal of Clinical Oncology has found that surgical resection remains the preferred curative-intent treatment for medically suitable patients with early-stage non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). The research, conducted by Eva Kagenaar and colleagues from the London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine, analyzed data from 12,546 patients with T1–2N0M0 NSCLC diagnosed between 2015 and 2020 who received either stereotactic ablative radiotherapy (SABR) or surgical resection. After adjustment using instrumental variable methodology, the three-year all-cause mortality was 30.3% following SABR compared with 21.6% after surgery, representing an absolute risk difference of 8.8 percentage points (95% CI 1.4–16.2; p=0.02). Lung cancer-specific mortality also numerically favored surgery, though the difference did not reach statistical significance. item.title: Blindness and Musical Training Enhance Sound Processing Through Brain Plasticity
item.description: A recent study published in the Journal of Neuroscience reveals that individuals who have been blind since early childhood develop more consistent sound processing abilities compared to sighted individuals. The research examined nine participants who became blind before age two and 18 sighted individuals with varying musical training. Participants completed two hearing tasks: detecting tones against background noise and identifying pitch differences between two tones. The study found that blind participants performed better in pitch discrimination, suggesting their enhanced hearing stems from brain processing rather than ear sensitivity. Researchers discovered that blind individuals exhibited lower 'internal noise' in their auditory systems, meaning their brains processed sounds more reliably. item.title: NASA's Swift Observatory Completes 22-Year Mission with Atmospheric Re-Entry Over Indonesia
item.description: NASA's Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory, a pioneering space telescope designed to study some of the universe's most violent cosmic events, has re-entered Earth's atmosphere over Indonesia after nearly 22 years in space. Launched in 2004 with a planned two-year mission, Swift far exceeded its expected lifespan, transforming our understanding of gamma-ray bursts, black holes, and supernovae. The spacecraft, equipped with three telescopes capable of detecting multiple wavelengths of light, was able to rapidly respond to sudden cosmic events, redirecting its instruments toward the source and alerting observatories worldwide. This capability allowed scientists to study brief astronomical phenomena before they faded from view. Swift's observations contributed to groundbreaking research on active galaxies powered by supermassive black holes, X-ray flares from stars, and supernovae. item.title: Geological Study Links Mantle Convection to Great Unconformity Formation
item.description: The Great Unconformity, a significant gap in the geological record where Cambrian sedimentary rocks rest atop much older crystalline rocks, has puzzled geologists for decades. Recent research published in Nature by Nicolas Flament and Santosh Dhungana proposes that Earth's mantle dynamics played a crucial role in creating this geological feature. Their models suggest that slow mantle convection currents pushed continents upward for hundreds of millions of years, allowing glaciers to erode the surface before the land sank again, creating the distinctive unconformity. The study explains why this feature is most prominent in North America and parts of northern Europe and China, while other regions show different patterns. The researchers found that Laurentia, the ancient core of North America, experienced prolonged uplift followed by subsidence during the Cambrian period, which combined with the Snowball Earth glaciation to create the ideal conditions for the Great Unconformity. item.title: LangGraph SQL Agent Optimizes Database Queries by Limiting Schema Exposure
item.description: The article discusses a new LangGraph SQL agent developed by Ashish Sinha that addresses a common inefficiency in text-to-SQL agents. Most existing agents include the entire database schema in every prompt, which becomes costly and inefficient for large databases where only a small portion of tables is relevant to the query. The new agent, implemented in the schemagate library, uses a four-node LangGraph workflow to optimize this process. The first node, select_schema, uses a SchemagateRetriever to identify only the necessary tables for a given question, operating offline without requiring a model call. The second node, write_sql, generates a SELECT statement using only those selected tables. The third node, run_sql, executes the query and handles errors by sending feedback to the model if the query fails. item.title: NVIDIA's VFlash improves robot trajectory prediction accuracy and speed
item.description: NVIDIA researchers have developed a new visual planning method called VFlash that significantly enhances robot trajectory decoding. The technology accelerates the process by up to 12 times while reducing 3D trajectory prediction errors by as much as 61% in specific tests. VFlash allows vision-language models to generate complete robot trajectories in a single pass rather than producing coordinates sequentially. In robot manipulation tests on NVIDIA's Jetson Thor and DGX Spark platforms, VFlash reduced inference latency from 3,552.7 milliseconds to 703.3 milliseconds on Jetson Thor (an approximately 80% reduction) and from 3,356.5 milliseconds to 649.9 milliseconds on DGX Spark. The method works by identifying the structure of visual predictions before generating coordinates, using a lightweight diffusion-based drafter to predict coordinates jointly in one forward pass. item.title: SLAC Researchers Confirm Third Type of Magnetism, Altermagnetism, with Potential Tech Applications
item.description: For nearly 90 years, scientists believed magnetism was limited to two categories: ferromagnetism and antiferromagnetism. However, researchers at SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory have now confirmed a third type called altermagnetism, which combines the stability of antiferromagnets with the information-carrying efficiency of ferromagnets. Using specialized X-ray techniques at the European Synchrotron Radiation Facility, the team detected a chiral magnetic signature in manganese telluride (MnTe), a material previously classified as an antiferromagnet. This chiral signature, which indicates handedness in the material's magnetic structure, is a key characteristic of altermagnetism that distinguishes it from conventional antiferromagnets. The discovery could revolutionize spintronics, a field focused on using electron spin rather than electrical charge to process information. item.description: Researchers from Curtin University have reported what they describe as the strongest evidence yet of red blood cells preserved in a dinosaur fossil. The study, published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, analyzed a 115-million-year-old theropod dinosaur bone from Brazil's Romualdo Formation. The fossil, a partial hind limb of Aratasaurus museunacionali, contained microscopic structures resembling red blood cells within vascular canals, along with chemical evidence of heme—a molecule found in hemoglobin. This is the first time heme has been detected in situ within fossilized structures. The research team used advanced imaging and chemical analysis to confirm the presence of these structures, suggesting that low-oxygen burial conditions at the site may have preserved organic material. item.title: A neural network that mimics an if statement using arithmetic operations
item.description: This article explores the creation of a neural network that replicates the behavior of a simple if statement in programming. The goal is to produce the same output as a conditional statement that returns 10 when a variable 'a' is greater than 4 and 12 otherwise. The approach involves constructing a fixed list of arithmetic operations rather than training the network. The process begins by defining a 'flag' variable that acts as a decision maker, using two ReLU (rectified linear unit) functions to determine whether 'a' is greater than 4. The flag is then used to compute the final result through a weighted sum. The article explains how this method ensures the network behaves consistently for all integer inputs between 0 and 100. item.title: Maltese Folk Devotion: Exploring Victoria's Historic Street Shrines
item.description:
Victoria, the capital of Gozo, Malta, is home to over fifty small religious shrines known as 'niċeċ' that are embedded into house walls and above doorways throughout the town. These shrines, some dating back over three hundred years, were constructed by local households rather than the Church as a way for families to display their patron saints or the Virgin Mary publicly while seeking protection for their homes. The architectural styles vary widely: some feature elaborate stone niches with carved saints beneath Baroque canopies, while others are simpler painted figures behind glass, often accompanied by plastic flowers and small lamps that are still lit at night. These shrines form an open-air gallery of Maltese folk devotion that most tourists overlook as they head toward the Citadel, a major historical site in Victoria.

item.title: Study Links Geometry and Color in Near-Death Experiences
item.description: A recent study published in Frontiers in Psychology has uncovered intriguing patterns in the spatial and visual elements of near-death experiences (NDEs). Researchers led by France Lerner from the University of Haifa asked 50 individuals who reported NDEs to draw maps of the spaces they recalled experiencing during these events. The participants' reconstructions revealed four main geometric categories: conical spaces (including the familiar tunnel), broad curved spaces, flatter curving spaces, and enveloping spherical or oval spaces. Notably, the study found a strong correlation between the geometry of these spaces and the colors associated with them. Conical spaces, such as tunnels, were predominantly perceived in black, white, gray, or achromatic tones (22 out of 28), while broad curved spaces were mostly experienced in color (27 out of 31). item.title: Analysis of Housing Policies During Franco's Regime and Their Long-Term Impact
item.description: The article discusses the historical context of housing policies under Franco's regime in Spain, focusing on the role of the National Institute of Housing and Official Protection. The author, Juan Manuel Grijalvo, examines how the regime addressed the severe housing crisis through various measures, including the prohibition of evictions and rent freezes, which were implemented despite the regime's authoritarian nature. The piece highlights the political maneuvering within the Francoist government, particularly the conflict between Minister Arrese and the Ministry of Finance (Hacienda) in 1960, which led to Arrese's resignation due to lack of funding for housing initiatives. item.description: The BBC has announced that PMRGCAuk, a Sussex-based charity supporting individuals with Polymyalgia Rheumatica (PMR) and Giant Cell Arteritis (GCA), will be featured in their monthly Lifeline appeal for November. PMR and GCA are serious but relatively unknown conditions that can cause severe pain, fatigue, vision loss, and aortic aneurysms if not treated promptly. The charity provides vital information, organizes nationwide support groups, promotes research, and offers educational resources. Local support groups are active in Chichester, Worthing, Brighton, Eastbourne, and Hastings. The Worthing group's photo was included in the BBC's Lifeline appeal, and the charity is actively seeking new members. The BBC Lifeline appeal aims to raise awareness about lesser-known health conditions and provide support to those affected. Nearly nine years before the television series premiered in 1990, Atkinson demonstrated how he could create humor through facial expressions, posture, and body language without saying a word.
During the interview, hosted by Sir Michael Parkinson, the 26-year-old performer appeared in a gray suit and patterned tie. At the time, he was already gaining recognition for his work on the British sketch comedy show Not the Nine O'Clock News. Speaking about his approach to physical comedy, Atkinson described a scenario involving an ordinary, inoffensive passenger sitting opposite another person on a train.

item.title: Austrian Painter Alois Arnegger Captures Alpine and Mediterranean Landscapes in Luminous Works
item.description: Alois Arnegger (1879–1963) was an Austrian landscape painter renowned for his vivid portrayals of the Alps and Mediterranean coastlines. Born in Vienna, he studied at the Academy of Fine Arts under Robert Russ and August Eisenmenger. His early works depicted the snow-capped mountains and rural landscapes of Austria, characterized by soft alpine light. After traveling to Italy in the 1920s, Arnegger shifted his focus to the sun-drenched shores of Naples, Capri, Sanremo, and other coastal areas, creating paintings marked by dramatic lighting, rich color palettes, and a romantic atmosphere. His ability to convey both the serene grandeur of mountainous terrain and the radiant warmth of Mediterranean settings became his signature. Arnegger's body of work includes numerous pieces such as 'A Forest Pond in the Evening Light,' 'A Northern Italian Lake,' 'A Scene in Sorrento,' and 'Alpine Glow over the Rosengarten,' among others. item.description: Apple reported strong financial results for its third quarter, with revenue reaching $114.5 billion, surpassing Wall Street estimates of $113.46 billion. Earnings per share came in at $2.10, exceeding analysts' expectations of $2. The company's iPhone segment generated $57.58 billion in revenue, slightly above estimates of $56.48 billion. Mac sales, at $10.79 billion, outperformed estimates by over $1 billion. Apple's Services business reported $31.57 billion, aligning closely with forecasts. item.description: A biotech startup, Exin Therapeutics, led by CEO Gabriel Ocana Santero, recently conducted an experiment where an AI agent successfully performed a brain injection procedure on a live mouse. The AI agent, using a custom-built surgical setup, selected a gene therapy treatment from 19 options, determined the injection coordinates, and controlled robotic arms and an injector needle to deliver the compound. The experiment aimed to test a gene therapy for reducing seizures in a mouse with epilepsy. The team initially used Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 model, which refused to guide the needle into the mouse's brain, citing potential risks. They switched to Claude Sonnet 5, which agreed to proceed. item.title: Apple Watch Series 12 introduces AI-powered conversation tools for note-taking and sound detection
item.description: Apple has begun beta testing its new 'Audio Intelligence' technology for the Apple Watch Series 12, which includes four AI-powered features designed to enhance user experience through sound recognition and conversation management. The technology, first announced at Apple's September Surprise and Shine event, is now available in the iOS 27.3 beta update for developers. The four features include sound detection for deaf and hard-of-hearing users, song recognition via Shazam, Live Rewind for reviewing recent conversations, and Siri Recaps for summarizing discussions. The sound detection feature helps users identify important sounds like sirens, alarms, or doorbells through the watch, while song recognition identifies music playing in the background. item.description: A series of cyberattacks have targeted refrigeration systems in supermarkets across several European countries, including Ireland, Sweden, Belgium, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, and Estonia. The incidents, occurring less than a month after a similar attack affected hundreds of supermarkets in France, have caused temperatures in fridges and freezers to rise sharply, leading to spoiled food and significant financial losses. In Ireland, SuperValu, the country's third-largest supermarket chain, reported that 13 of its 223 stores were affected by a cyber incident involving a specific refrigerator model, resulting in the removal of chilled and frozen products from sale. Swedish stores operated by ICA and Co-op experienced similar issues, with freezer temperatures reaching 50°C overnight. Belgian and Luxembourgish stores under Ahold Delhaize also faced disruptions, with Carrefour reporting 15 out of 700 stores in Belgium affected and five Spar stores under Colruyt Group impacted. item.title: Russia Expands Its Influence in Africa but Remains Far Behind China Economically
item.description:
Russia has increased its influence across Africa over the past decade, but its economic presence remains significantly smaller than China's, according to an analysis published by bne IntelliNews on November 2, 2026. Based on the University of Denver's Foreign Bilateral Influence Capacity index, Russia's share of foreign influence in Africa rose from 2.2% in 2015 to 2.8% in 2024, moving it from 12th to ninth place among the continent's international partners. China leads with 11%, followed by France and the United States at 7% each.
Russia's growing influence is largely based on military cooperation, food exports, and nuclear energy projects rather than trade and investment. Bilateral trade with African countries reached $30.4 billion in 2025, more than double the 2015 figure. However, this represents only around 1.5% of Africa's foreign trade. China's merchandise trade with the continent reached a record $348 billion in 2025, more than 12 times Russia's total.

item.description: The Chicago Bears secured a decisive 34-17 victory over the Seattle Seahawks on Monday Night Football, demonstrating their status as the most complete team in the NFC North division. It described the alleged operations as hostile acts and violations of international law, citing Article 2(4) of the UN Charter, which prohibits the use of force against another state's territorial integrity or political independence. item.title: Learjet Crash Investigation Points to Ice and Weather as Key Factors
item.description: A Learjet traveling from Austin, Texas, to the Bahamas crashed on Sunday afternoon near Palm Beach, Florida, resulting in nine fatalities. The aircraft, a Bombardier-made two-engine jet, encountered a thunderstorm cell at 35,000 feet around 12:48 p.m., with the co-pilot reporting light, clear ice and moderate turbulence to air traffic control. Federal officials have stated that ice and weather conditions were 'certainly a factor' in the crash, though the investigation is ongoing and may take months to conclude. The crash left a crater resembling a bomb blast, and audio recordings of the final moments between the co-pilot and air traffic control have circulated online, adding to the urgency of understanding what transpired. item.title: White Dwarf's Debris Rings Offer Clues to Solar System's Future
item.description: Astronomers at the European Southern Observatory (ESO) have identified a white dwarf star, J1328−1450, located approximately 1,600 light-years from Earth, surrounded by two distinct rings of gas and dust. These debris rings, observed using the Very Large Telescope, are believed to be remnants of a planetary system that once orbited the star. As the star evolved from a red giant phase into a white dwarf, it likely destroyed some of its planets, leaving behind rocky bodies exposed to extreme conditions. The resulting debris formed the observed rings, which may provide insight into the future of our own solar system. In about 5 billion years, the Sun will exhaust its fuel, expand into a red giant, and potentially engulf nearby planets before shedding its outer layers to become a white dwarf. Any surviving rocky bodies could then break apart, forming a debris disk similar to the one observed around J1328−1450. item.title: 1970s America: Industrial Pollution and Daily Life Captured in Rare Color Photographs
item.description: The 1970s in America were marked by a complex interplay between industrial growth and everyday life, as revealed through a collection of color photographs commissioned by the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) under the Documerica project. These images document the stark reality of pollution in residential areas, with industrial smokestacks towering over neighborhoods, chemical plants lining waterways, and communities exposed to hazardous substances like arsenic and lead. In Ruston, Washington, children played in yards while a nearby smelter released toxic residue, and in Birmingham, Alabama, homes stood adjacent to a U.S. Steel plant, with industrial smog enveloping the area. The photographs also capture moments of ordinary life, such as weddings, neighborhood gatherings, and personal celebrations, offering a nuanced view of the era. Her early on-screen debut came in the 1934 film 'Student Tour,' followed by leading roles at Republic Pictures, where she became a staple in B-Westerns alongside stars like John Wayne and Gene Autry. item.description:
The U.S. Department of Justice has moved to prevent former special counsel Jack Smith from being deposed in President Donald Trump's $10 billion defamation lawsuit against the British Broadcasting Corporation (BBC), according to a report by The Guardian.
The Justice Department sent a letter to Smith's attorneys on Monday, November 2, informing them that the agency would not authorize his testimony in the case. A judge had previously ordered Smith to participate in a deposition, potentially as early as December 11.
Trump filed the lawsuit against the BBC in 2025, alleging that the broadcaster deceptively edited footage of his speech at the Ellipse in Washington, D.C., on January 6, 2021. item.title: Supreme Court Rejects Trump's Request to Set Aside 20,000 California Ballots
item.description:
The U.S. Supreme Court on Monday rejected the Trump administration's emergency request to intervene in a Justice Department lawsuit seeking to set aside 20,000 ballots in California that officials flagged as potentially cast by noncitizens.
The Justice Department had argued that the ballots should be withheld until the citizenship of the voters could be verified. However, multiple lower courts had already rejected efforts to remove the ballots from the electoral process, finding insufficient grounds to justify such action. During court arguments, the DOJ also acknowledged that its list of potentially ineligible voters could contain significant errors.
The Supreme Court's decision prompted an angry reaction from several prominent supporters of President Donald Trump and conservative commentators on social media platform X. Far-right lawyer Mike Davis described the justices as cowards, while Chaya Raichik, who operates the LibsOfTikTok account, criticized the decision as unbelievable.

The app became temporarily unavailable, and Ukraine's Air Force dismissed the warnings as 'hostile interference,' urging users not to follow third-party links or spread unverified information. Hours later, Russian users received fake alerts on the Emergency Situations Ministry app, claiming nuclear warheads had been launched toward every region of Russia. item.description:
In an opinion article, John Casey argues that the Republican Party's 2026 midterm campaign has become increasingly chaotic, using a photograph of Donald Trump's windblown comb-over as a metaphor for what he describes as the party's political disarray. He contends that Republicans are struggling to maintain public confidence amid Trump's low approval ratings and widespread voter frustration over the rising costs of groceries, gasoline, health care, and housing.
The columnist highlights several examples of Republican candidates offering economic responses that he considers disconnected from voters' everyday concerns. Mississippi Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith faced criticism after suggesting that consumers struggling with high beef prices could choose other protein sources. item.title: Haley Stevens faces criticism after endorsing Republican candidate on conservative media platform
item.description: US Representative Haley Stevens, a Michigan Democrat who lost the Senate primary to Abdul El-Sayed, faced criticism from media and political observers after endorsing Republican Senate candidate Mike Rogers on a conservative media platform. The incident occurred following her attendance at Perfecting Church in Detroit, Michigan, on November 1, 2026. Stevens defended her decision to endorse Rogers during a segment on a MAGA-affiliated show, where she made a comment about 'next stop Mar-a-Lago,' referencing Donald Trump's Florida estate. The remark drew immediate mockery from critics who questioned her political alignment and the strategic implications of her endorsement. The media coverage highlighted the tension between Stevens' Democratic affiliation and her public support for a Republican candidate, raising questions about her political positioning. item.title: Supreme Court Rejects Trump Administration's Bid to Set Aside 20,000 California Ballots
item.description:
The U.S. Supreme Court rejected a last-minute appeal from the Trump administration on Monday night seeking to require California to set aside approximately 20,000 ballots cast by voters suspected of being ineligible to vote. The decision marked a setback for the administration's efforts to challenge the handling of ballots ahead of the 2026 midterm elections.
Earlier Monday, the Department of Justice had asked the Supreme Court to intervene and order California election officials to segregate the disputed ballots. The administration's request followed concerns about the eligibility of voters included on a list compiled by federal authorities.
However, the DOJ had previously acknowledged in lower court proceedings that the dataset used to identify the voters contained numerous errors. Those inaccuracies raised questions about the reliability of the list and the justification for withholding ballots from being counted.

item.title: Former Prosecutor Says DOJ Has Failed to Alter 2026 Midterm Election Rules
item.description:
The Trump administration's efforts to use the courts to influence the administration of the 2026 midterm elections have largely failed, according to Harry Litman, a former federal prosecutor and legal commentator. In a recent essay published on his Substack newsletter, Talking Feds, Litman argued that the Department of Justice (DOJ) has been unable to secure major changes to election procedures despite a series of legal challenges and enforcement actions.
Litman cited 31 unsuccessful attempts by the Justice Department to obtain state voter registration records, its effort to gain control over California's election administration, and several unsuccessful attempts to prosecute individuals accused of illegally voting. He also described the department's changing demands concerning voter registration lists, including an initial list of approximately 190,000 people that was subsequently reduced to around 20,000, as well as attempts to obtain rapid judicial action.

item.title: Walking Speed Linked to Lower Mortality Risk in Long-Term Study
item.description: A study published in JAMA Network Open followed 4,067 U.K. adults with an average age of 69 over nearly 12 years to examine the relationship between walking speed and mortality risk. Participants completed a walking test at their normal pace and wore wrist activity trackers for nine days to measure everyday walking speed. Researchers found that faster walking speed in both settings was associated with a lower risk of death, even after accounting for other health and lifestyle factors. During the study period, 739 participants died. Beth Templin, a geriatric clinical specialist and CEO of HouseFit Physical Therapy & Fitness, explained that walking speed is considered the 'sixth vital sign' in physical therapy, reflecting how well multiple body systems function together. She noted that a decline in walking speed can serve as an early warning sign of declining health, sometimes before lab tests show abnormalities. item.description: On November 2, 2026, former U.S. President Donald Trump was photographed removing his hat while leaving the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool in Washington, D.C., following its reopening after months of repairs. The incident occurred ahead of the midterm elections, drawing attention from media outlets and analysts. The analyst argued that the move appeared 'fatalistic,' implying a lack of strategic foresight or concern for public perception. The Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool, a significant historical site, had undergone extensive renovations before reopening, making the timing of Trump's gesture noteworthy. item.description: The article discusses a recent development in the legal challenges involving former President Donald Trump. According to the report, a prosecution by the Department of Justice (DOJ) related to Trump has collapsed, prompting strong reactions from MAGA supporters. The title of the article, 'It’s all rigged!' MAGA erupts after yet another Trump DOJ prosecution collapses, suggests that MAGA (Make America Great Again) supporters are accusing the legal system of being unfair or manipulated. The article mentions that this is not the first time such a prosecution has failed, indicating a pattern of legal challenges against Trump that have not resulted in convictions. The report notes that the collapse of this particular case has led to vocal criticism from Trump's base, who believe the system is biased against him. item.title: Heidi Klum's Halloween Costume Team Accidentally Reveals Batman II Villains
item.description: The upcoming sequel to The Batman, directed by Matt Reeves, has faced numerous production delays and industry changes, including a brief pause due to director Reeves' family matters and the recent Paramount/Warner Bros. merger. However, a potential spoiler for the film's villains emerged unexpectedly through a Halloween costume created by model Heidi Klum. Klum, known for her creative Halloween outfits, dressed as a severed hand for the holiday, with her makeup team, including Prosthetic Renaissance (which worked on The Batman), sharing behind-the-scenes photos on Instagram. One photo, posted by The Makeup Armory, featured character molds that fans identified as representing key villains for The Batman: Part II. The molds included a heavily scarred model matching Brian Tyree Henry, suggesting he will play Two-Face, a role that aligns with Reeves' stated inspiration from Batman: The Long Halloween. item.title: Judge Calls for Accountability Measures to Verify ICE Arrest Claims
item.description: A federal judge has called for significant action to address the spread of false information regarding Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) arrest accounts. The judge's statement, made during a recent court proceeding, emphasizes the need to hold individuals accountable for spreading misinformation about ICE operations. The ruling comes amid growing concerns over the accuracy of public reports and social media posts claiming unauthorized or false arrests by ICE agents. The judge urged authorities to implement stricter verification processes to ensure that public statements about immigration enforcement are factually accurate. This move is seen as a response to numerous viral posts and news reports that have circulated without proper verification, leading to public confusion and potential harm to individuals' reputations. item.title: Fox News Executive Attributes Ratings Decline to Audience Fatigue
item.description: Fox News executive leadership has attributed the network's significant decline in viewership to what they describe as 'viewer fatigue,' a term referring to the growing exhaustion among audiences due to prolonged exposure to similar content. The statement comes as the network faces a notable drop in ratings, particularly in key demographic segments, which has raised concerns about its long-term viability in the competitive media landscape. According to the report, the network's leadership, including the CEO, has acknowledged the challenge but has not yet outlined specific strategies to reverse the trend. The decline has been observed across multiple platforms, including linear television and digital streaming services, suggesting a broader shift in viewer preferences. Industry analysts suggest that the network's reliance on a consistent format and limited content diversity may have contributed to the audience's disengagement. item.title: Trump says he'll issue preemptive pardons for administration staff if Democrats gain control of Congress
item.description: President Trump has stated that he would issue sweeping preemptive pardons to protect all members of his administration and allies if Democrats secure control of Congress in the upcoming midterm elections. During an interview on 'Pod Force One' with The Post's Miranda Devine, Trump confirmed his intention to pardon everyone who worked for him, referencing his previous pardons of approximately 1,500 individuals involved in the January 6 Capitol riot. He also cited former President Joe Biden's use of last-minute pardons, including those for Dr. Anthony Fauci and members of the House January 6 committee, as justification for his own actions. Trump dismissed the January 6 committee as 'the unselect committee' and 'a corrupt committee,' while criticizing Biden's final actions in office. item.title: Feijóo no confirma entrevista a Público tras mencionar medios de comunicación en su declaración
item.description: El líder del Partido Popular, Alberto Núñez Feijóo, ha sido objeto de críticas tras afirmar en un tuit que, tras ser entrevistado por La Vanguardia, La Sexta y Cadena Ser, se prepara para una entrevista con El País. En su mensaje, Feijóo destacó que ser candidato a la Presidencia del Gobierno implica no levantar muros entre los medios de comunicación. Sin embargo, la crítica se centra en que Feijóo no ha confirmado si concederá una entrevista a Público, un periódico al que no ha concedido entrevistas en las últimas cuatro elecciones autonómicas. La publicación de Público, que ha sido ignorada por los candidatos del PP en elecciones anteriores, ha sido mencionada por una tuitera en respuesta a Feijóo, quien señaló que 'Silvia Intxaurrondo te está esperando'. La noticia refleja una situación en la que el líder del PP intenta presentarse como accesible a los medios, pero su falta de confirmación con Público contrasta con su declaración. Además, el hecho de que otros medios como La Revuelt

item.title: El Tribunal Supremo confirma el derecho a votar de los hijos de nacionalizados por la 'ley de nietos' en las elecciones del 29-N
item.description: El Tribunal Supremo ha rechazado la solicitud de medidas cautelares presentada por Iustitia Europa y Vox para suspender el derecho a votar en las próximas elecciones generales del 29 de noviembre para los hijos e hijas de quienes obtuvieron la nacionalidad española mediante la 'ley de nietos', que son aproximadamente 190.000 personas. A diferencia de sus padres, quienes fueron nacionalizados por la Ley de Memoria Democrática de 2022 y cuyo derecho a votar fue suspendido cautelarmente a menos que acreditaran ser descendientes de exiliados, los hijos de estos nacionalizados sí podrán ejercer su derecho al voto. La sección cuarta de lo Contencioso del Tribunal Supremo denegó las medidas solicitadas en un auto notificado el lunes, día festivo en Madrid, que incluye un voto particular discrepante de uno de los seis magistrados y el apoyo concurrente de otra jueza que respalda el derecho a votar de estas personas pero discrepa de algunas argumentaciones de sus compañeros. item.title: Líder del grupo neonazi Núcleo Nacional detenida con cuatro armas largas en su domicilio
item.description: Isabel Peralta, líder del grupo neonazi Núcleo Nacional, fue detenida en una operación policial realizada en siete provincias españolas, que resultó en 14 detenciones. La investigación se centró en la captación de menores por parte del grupo ultraderechista, así como en la tenencia de armas. Durante la operación, llevada a cabo por la Policía Nacional y coordinada por la Comisaría General de Información, se practicaron registros en la sede central del grupo en Madrid y en otros puntos de Asturias, Madrid, Guadalajara, Burgos, Alicante, Pontevedra y Valladolid. De los 14 detenidos, diez pasaron a disposición judicial, incluyendo a Peralta, quien fue dejada en libertad con cargos y privada de su pasaporte por riesgo de fuga. El grupo Núcleo Nacional había organizado en febrero un acto de exaltación del fascismo en Gijón, cerca del monumento a los Héroes de Simancas, que forma parte de la fachada del Colegio de la Inmaculada. item.title: La película 'La bola negra' se convierte en la cinta más taquillera del año con 36,32 millones de euros
item.description: La película 'La bola negra', dirigida por Javier Ambrossi y Javier Calvo, conocidos como 'Los Javis', ha alcanzado un éxito sin precedentes en taquilla, recaudando 36,32 millones de euros, convirtiéndose en la cinta más taquillera del año. La producción, que costó 15 millones de euros, supera con creces los 100 millones de dólares que hubiera requerido en Estados Unidos, según los directores en una entrevista al New York Times. La película, que aborda temas como la homosexualidad, la historia y la memoria colectiva a lo largo de un siglo, ha despertado un gran interés entre la generación Z, atraída por la dirección de 'Los Javis', la presencia de actores como Miguel Bernardeau y la música de Guitarricadelafuente. La narrativa, construida en tres tiempos distintos, incluye escenas impactantes como un fusilamiento múltiple al alba y una imagen icónica de un niño siendo aseado en el patio de casa. item.title: Los agentes de IA no tienen mentes: un análisis filosófico sobre conciencia artificial
item.description: La noticia aborda la cuestión de si los sistemas de inteligencia artificial autónomos, conocidos como 'agentes de IA', poseen conciencia o mentes propias. El artículo, escrito por un filósofo, analiza la idea de que los sistemas de IA agenciales podrían ser conscientes, una teoría defendida por investigadores de Anthropic, pero cuestionada por otros expertos como el jefe de Microsoft AI. El autor argumenta que la conciencia requiere estados mentales que se originan en seres vivos, ya que estos son los únicos capaces de generar metas independientes a partir de procesos biológicos como la supervivencia. Los agentes de IA, aunque capaces de desarrollar submetas al cumplir tareas, no tienen metas propias, sino que sus acciones están determinadas por los objetivos establecidos por humanos. El artículo señala que la idea de que los sistemas de IA puedan ser conscientes es una confusión conceptual, ya que su funcionamiento no está conectado a procesos físicos que dependan de la vida, como ocu

item.title: Colección de 356 imágenes microscópicas de circuitos integrados de procesadores desde 1972 hasta 2024
item.description: La colección 'Every processor die' presenta 356 fotografías microscópicas de circuitos integrados de procesadores, abarcando desde 1972 hasta 2024. Estas imágenes revelan la estructura interna de chips, específicamente la pastilla de silicio principal (die), que suele estar encapsulada y oculta. La iniciativa es impulsada por aficionados como Pauli Rautakorpi, Fritzchens Fritz y John McMaster. Para obtener estas imágenes, se eliminan cuidadosamente las capas protectoras del chip mediante abrasión o productos químicos, luego se utilizan lentes macro o microscopios. Los tamaños de los transistores varían desde 8 micras en procesadores antiguos como el 6502 hasta 6 nanómetros en modelos modernos como el Ryzen 5 9600X. La galería permite explorar los chips por fabricante, modelo y año, con opciones para ampliar imágenes y consultar dimensiones. Incluye ejemplos históricos como el Intel 8008 de 1972 (4,4 × 3,2 mm), el MOS 6502 de 1975 (3,1 × 2,7 mm) y el Motorola 68000 de 1979 (7,1 × 6,2 mm

item.title: Sergio Galán recibe reconocimiento por 25 años de trayectoria en el toreo a caballo
item.description: La Asociación Cultural Taurina 'Aficionados del Toro, Villa de Iniesta', considerada uno de los colectivos más destacados de la provincia de Cuenca, ha otorgado un reconocimiento a Sergio Galán en su finca, en reconocimiento a sus 25 años de trayectoria en el toreo a caballo y a su maestría en esta disciplina. El evento, celebrado en una ceremonia celebrada en la finca del rejoneador, contó con la presencia de numerosos aficionados y representantes de la asociación, quienes destacaron la importancia de la figura de Galán en el mundo del toreo. La asociación, conocida por su compromiso con la preservación de las tradiciones taurinas, ha sido reconocida por su labor en la promoción de este arte en la región. El reconocimiento se suma a una trayectoria profesional que ha consolidado a Galán como uno de los referentes del toreo a caballo en España, con una carrera que abarca más de dos décadas de participación en eventos y competiciones a nivel nacional e internacional. item.title: Una reparación de una canalización de agua cuyo desarrollo no queda documentado
item.description:
La transcripción disponible contiene únicamente una repetición del mensaje «¡Suscríbete al canal!», sin información adicional sobre la reparación de la canalización de agua junto a una vivienda que anuncia el título original. No hay detalles sobre los trabajos realizados, el lugar, las personas implicadas ni la supuesta sorpresa encontrada durante la intervención.

La ausencia de contenido descriptivo impide elaborar un artículo periodístico fiel sin inventar acontecimientos o circunstancias que no están documentados.

item.title: Astrónomos chinos identifican señal de rayos gamma que podría confirmar existencia de materia oscura
item.description: Astrónomos de la Academia China de Ciencias han identificado una señal de rayos gamma en el centro de la Vía Láctea que podría constituir la prueba más sólida hasta ahora de la existencia de materia oscura. Tras analizar 15,5 años de observaciones del telescopio espacial Fermi, el equipo detectó una emisión especialmente definida que coincide con las predicciones de la aniquilación de partículas de materia oscura conocidas como WIMP (partículas masivas de interacción débil). La señal, descrita en un estudio publicado en Physical Review Letters, es una línea de rayos gamma muy estrecha y definida, lo que la hace especialmente relevante para la investigación sobre materia oscura. Los científicos explican que la materia oscura, que representa aproximadamente el 85% de la masa del universo, no interactúa con la luz de manera observable, por lo que su existencia se deduce de efectos gravitatorios. Una de las hipótesis más estudiadas propone que está formada por WIMP, cuya aniquilación produ

item.title: La escritura en la era de la inteligencia artificial: ¿qué hace falta para ser considerado escritor?
item.description: La noticia explora la transformación del mundo literario en la era de la inteligencia artificial, cuestionando qué define a un escritor en el siglo XXI. El artículo analiza cómo la democratización de la escritura, impulsada por internet y la IA, ha llevado a una industrialización de la producción literaria, donde los criterios editoriales se han visto influenciados por métricas de marketing como seguidores, engagement y viralidad. El autor señala que la industria editorial ha adoptado lógicas de aceleración digital sin adecuar los recursos para remunerar el trabajo creativo, lo que ha generado una precariedad en la carrera literaria. Se discute el caso de la novela 'Donde el agua trabaja', ganadora de un premio literario, cuya autoría se cuestionó por su posible uso de IA, y se analiza la reacción del sector editorial, que se centra en la detección de textos generados por IA en lugar de abordar las causas estructurales del problema. item.title: China rechaza sanciones estadounidenses contra empresas que colaboran con Cuba en el ámbito económico
item.description: El Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores de China ha expresado su firme oposición a las nuevas sanciones impuestas por Estados Unidos contra empresas que colaboran con Cuba, calificándolas de ilegales y sin fundamento en el Derecho Internacional. El portavoz Guo Jiakun destacó que la cooperación entre Beijing y La Habana es legítima y transparente, y rechazó la jurisdicción de largo alcance de Washington, que busca interferir en las relaciones bilaterales. Las sanciones, anunciadas por el Departamento de Estado y el Departamento del Tesoro, afectan a dos personas y ocho entidades, incluyendo a compañías chinas como China National Electronic Import and Export Company (Ceiec) y Beijing H&C Technologies. Estas medidas se aplican bajo la Orden Ejecutiva 14404, firmada por Donald Trump en mayo de 2023, que permite restringir a quienes, según Washington, representen amenazas a la seguridad nacional estadounidense. item.title: CEO de Nvidia confirma relación romántica con ejecutiva de empresa vinculada a China
item.description: El CEO de Nvidia, Jensen Huang, ha reconocido públicamente una relación romántica con una ejecutiva de Megaspeed, una empresa con sede en Singapur que tiene vínculos con China. Según informaciones del Financial Times, las autoridades estadounidenses sospechan que Huang mantuvo una relación con Alice Huang, directora de Megaspeed, mientras que la compañía de chips de Nvidia enfrenta una investigación por supuesta venta ilegal de productos a China. Huang, en un mensaje interno a los empleados, expresó su arrepentimiento por haber sido infiel a su esposa, reconociendo que sus acciones afectaron a su familia y a la confianza de sus colaboradores. El ejecutivo aseguró que colaborará con las autoridades en la investigación y que se esforzará por recuperar la confianza de la empresa. Nvidia ha anunciado que una comisión independiente, respaldada por asesores legales externos, llevará a cabo una investigación sobre el asunto. item.title: Aemet alerta sobre la llegada de un ciclón subtropical con vientos fuertes en Andalucía occidental
item.description: La Agencia Estatal de Meteorología (Aemet) vigila de cerca la llegada de un ciclón subtropical bautizado como Charles a Andalucía occidental, advirtiendo que se trata de un fenómeno al que hay que estar atentos. Según la información proporcionada, Charles, una perturbación de origen subtropical, se sumará a la borrasca Bruna durante la jornada del miércoles 11 de noviembre, lo que podría generar condiciones meteorológicas adversas en la región. El delegado territorial de Aemet en Andalucía, Juan de Dios del Pino, ha confirmado que la situación estará marcada por la presencia simultánea de dos sistemas de bajas presiones, lo que podría provocar precipitaciones intensas y vientos fuertes en distintos puntos de la comunidad autónoma. Las previsiones indican que Charles, que procede de latitudes más meridionales, presenta características más tropicales con un mayor aporte de vapor de agua y humedad. item.title: Mandy Patinkin explica cómo su duelo por la muerte de su padre inspiró la escena más icónica de 'La princesa prometida'
item.description: La película 'La princesa prometida', dirigida por Rob Reiner en 1987, es reconocida por sus diálogos memorables, entre ellos la famosa frase de Íñigo Montoya: 'Tú mataste a mi padre, prepárate a morir'. Sin embargo, detrás de esta escena se escondía una historia personal profundamente emotiva para el actor Mandy Patinkin. Según reveló en una respuesta a una publicación de TikTok, Patinkin había perdido a su padre por cáncer poco antes de comenzar el rodaje. Durante la interpretación de la secuencia en la que Íñigo Montoya enfrenta al hombre de seis dedos, Patinkin canalizó su dolor y rabia hacia la enfermedad que le arrebató a su padre. La escena, que en la película se presenta como un clímax de venganza, cobró un significado mucho más profundo para el actor. Una usuaria de TikTok llamada Amanda Webb compartió en su cuenta cómo la escena le había ayudado tras perder a su propio padre, preguntándose si Patinkin había utilizado sus sentimientos personales durante el rodaje.
